title: Tech rally lifts stock futures to wrap up a volatile week of trading
html:
Hello, this is Leonie Kidd with today's edition of Morning Squawk.

The Thanksgiving cheer is extending into the market this Friday, with a relief rally across the tech sector after a volatile week of trading.

The half-day session looks set to be driven by those buying the dip in some of the biggest AI names.

Stock futures are rising as Wall Street prepares to open higher following a volatile week for technology stocks.

It's a shortened trading day following Thanksgiving, but the bulls are out, with S&P 500 futures up nearly 2%, while Nasdaq-100 futures advanced 2.3%. Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average were higher by around 1%.

But the devil is in the data. On Thursday, President Donald Trump used his Thanksgiving message on Truth Social to falsely claim that the latest GDP revision was a "record-setting error" that therefore had to be "immediately investigated."

The second reading of third-quarter GDP on Wednesday showed a 4.3% annualized growth rate, revised up from the initial estimate of 3.4%.

  • Trump's Truth Social: "HAPPY THANKSGIVING TO ALL AMERICAN PATRIOTS WHO HAVE WORKED SO HARD TO MAKE OUR COUNTRY GREAT! Additionally, I would like to wish a Happy Thanksgiving to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%, A RECORD SETTING ERROR, and one so grave that it should be immediately investigated..."
  • Analysis: As CNBC's Steve Leisman and Sean Conlon report, the difference between the advance estimate and the figure in the second release is far from being an all-time record, adding that "on an absolute basis, the latest revision was tied for 16th among all revisions from the advance estimate to the second release since 1990."
  • Why it matters: Traders are already pricing in a near-100% chance of a hike at the Fed's December meeting, with the latest data providing more evidence of the economy's resilience to potential further increases.

The technology sector is leading gains in premarket trading.

The Magnificent Seven, alongside chip-related stocks, neoclouds and server makers are all trading higher.

Nvidia is up over 4%, alongside Anthropic, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and others.

There was a sharp rebound overnight for Chinese stocks, with the country's chip-makers notching their biggest-ever one-day gains.

  • Pro: A 170-year historical study indicates a "major market collapse" is coming. Find out why this research suggests, "The artificial intelligence boom is flashing signs of speculative excess that rival those seen at the height of the dot-com bubble," here.

SpaceX shares are higher in premarket trading after Elon Musk posted on X.com that he was expanding his share-donation plan for American children.

He said, "I will be donating another share of SpaceX to all kids in America every year." It comes alongside the group's commitment to allocate one SpaceX share to each active Trump Account.

  • Space competition: CNBC's Elsa Ohlen reports that Europe's largest satellite factory has been inaugurated in Belgium this week, as the continent looks to challenge Elon Musk's Starlink dominance and reduce its reliance on America for space infrastructure.

CNBC's Kai Nicol-Schwarz has published two scoops this week about the impact of the Trump administration's tightening of restrictions on Chinese remote access to Nvidia chips.

First up, he reports that neocloud firms are being told they cannot purchase Nvidia chips if any of that computing capacity would be rented to Chinese companies. That's according to sources.

  • Why it matters: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC that new Commerce rules were being implemented to close "loopholes" and reduce indirect access to U.S.-made chips.

Secondly, the sellers of Nvidia chips are seeking new buyers as they look to find new homes for GPUs that were originally for use in data centers through which Chinese companies would rent access.

  • Why it matters: Sources suggest that an unusually high supply of Nvidia GPUs has been offered for sale since the rule was announced.
  • What's next: Kai says, "I've spent most of my week asking sources how the crackdown on Chinese companies accessing Nvidia chips remotely will impact the whole supply chain. This is a long-tail story that no doubt has a way to play out."

Texture-maxxing is the latest food trend taking social media by storm as consumers, driven by aesthetics and taste, look for a sensory experience.

British supermarket Waitrose's latest food and drink report highlighted "texture-maxxing" as one of the trends of the year. It describes the phenomenon as a multi-sensory indulgence that is "fuelled by texture-maxxing crunch and intense flavour hits," pushing shoppers to fill their trolleys with crunchy peanut butter, dumplings, and trifles.

— CNBC's Jenni Reid, Lee Ying Shan, Steve Liesman, Sean Conlon, Jenyn Lee, Elsa Ohlen, Kai Nicol-Schwarz and Sawdah Bhaimiya contributed to this report.

Jack Sommers edited this edition.
summary: President Trump demands a probe into the GDP revision data.
